## Introduction

`ReLTER.inatEnrich` is a companion module for the
[ReLTER](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16927384) package. It extends the
core ReLTER functionality by enriching iNaturalist biodiversity occurrence
records — downloaded for a specific eLTER-RI site — with a set of
conservation and legal attributes:

- **Nativeness / establishment means** (native, introduced, etc.) sourced
  from iNaturalist checklists, filtered by country, and cross-referenced
  with the [EASIN](https://easin.jrc.ec.europa.eu/easin) (European Alien
  Species Information Network) database for additional alien species
  information
- **IUCN Red List conservation status** at global and regional level,
  directly as recorded on iNaturalist
- **EU legal framework** coverage under the Habitats Directive
  (92/43/EEC) and the Birds Directive (2009/147/EC), retrieved from the
  [EUNIS](https://eunis.eea.europa.eu/) species database

The final output is a fully enriched occurrence dataset and an interactive
Leaflet map summarising all information in observation-level popups.

---

## Requirements

The following packages must be installed before using `ReLTER.inatEnrich`:

```{r requirements}
# Core dependencies
install.packages(c(
  "dplyr",
  "purrr",
  "httr2",
  "sf",
  "leaflet",
  "ggplot2",
  "grDevices",
  "rinat",
  "rvest",
  "stats"
))

# ReLTER — the parent package providing site info and occurrence download
# https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16927384
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("eLTER-RI/ReLTER")

# ReLTER.inatEnrich — this package
remotes::install_github("eLTER-RI/ReLTER.inatEnrich")
```

Then load the packages:

```{r load}
library(ReLTER)
library(ReLTER.inatEnrich)
```

---

## What is a DEIMS-ID?

The **DEIMS-ID** (Dynamic Ecological Information Management System – Site
and dataset registry ID) is a unique and persistent identifier assigned to
each site registered in the
[DEIMS-SDR](https://deims.org) registry — the central catalogue of
eLTER-RI research sites.

A DEIMS-ID takes the form of a resolvable URL, for example:

```
https://deims.org/6b62feb2-61bf-47e1-b97f-0e909c408db8
```

You can browse registered sites at [deims.org](https://deims.org) and
copy the DEIMS-ID from the site page. It is the entry point for all
ReLTER functions: it allows the package to retrieve site boundaries,
country information, and linked datasets from a single, unambiguous
identifier.

For more information see the
[DEIMS-ID documentation](https://deims.org/docs/deimsid.html).

---

## Workflow

The enrichment pipeline consists of seven steps, illustrated below.

```{r workflow-diagram, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "ReLTER.inatEnrich enrichment workflow."}
# If you have a workflow diagram image, place it in vignettes/figures/ and
# reference it here, e.g.:
# knitr::include_graphics("figures/workflow.png")
```

### Step 1 — Define the eLTER-RI site

Set the DEIMS-ID of the target eLTER-RI site. In this example we use the
**Montagna di Torricchio** site (Italy).

```{r step1}
deimsid <- "https://deims.org/6b62feb2-61bf-47e1-b97f-0e909c408db8"
```

### Step 2 — Download iNaturalist occurrences

Download all iNaturalist observations associated with the eLTER-RI site
using [`ReLTER::get_site_speciesOccurrences()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/ReLTER/reference/get_site_speciesOccurrences.html).
The `limit` argument caps the maximum number of records returned.

```{r step2}
iNat_occ_eLTER_site <- ReLTER::get_site_speciesOccurrences(
  deimsid  = deimsid,
  list_DS  = "inat",
  show_map = TRUE,
  limit    = 5000
)
```

### Step 3 — Retrieve site boundary and country

Download the site boundary polygon and extract the country name. The
country is used in the following step to filter establishment means to
the correct national checklist.

```{r step3}
site_boundary <- ReLTER::get_site_info(deimsid = deimsid)
country <- site_boundary$country
```

### Step 4 — Add IUCN conservation status

`add_iucn_to_occ()` queries [iNaturalist](https://forum.inaturalist.org/t/updating-iucn-red-list-conservation-statuses/25712)
for each unique taxon and appends a nested `status_IUCN` list-column. Each
element is a tibble with one row per geographic scope (global, regional),
containing the IUCN status code, authority, scope name, and a direct link
to the [IUCN Red List assessment](https://www.iucnredlist.org).

```{r step4}
occ_eLTER_IUCN <- add_iucn_to_occ(occ_eLTER = iNat_occ_eLTER_site$inat)
```

```
# Example content of status_IUCN[[1]]:
# A tibble: 3 × 4
#   status authority      scope_of_assesment url
#   <chr>  <chr>          <chr>              <chr>
# 1 LC     IUCN Red List  Globally           https://www.iucnredlist.org/...
# 2 LC     IUCN Red List  Europe             https://www.iucnredlist.org/...
# 3 LC     IUCN Red List  Mediterranean      https://www.iucnredlist.org/...
```

### Step 5 — Add nativeness / establishment means and EASIN data

`add_nativeness_to_occ()` enriches each unique taxon with two complementary
sources of alien species information:

**From iNaturalist checklists** — the
[establishment means](https://help.inaturalist.org/en/support/solutions/articles/151000176171-how-to-add-or-edit-establishment-means-in-inaturalist)
of each taxon (following the
[Darwin Core Vocabulary](https://dwc.tdwg.org/em/) definition) is
retrieved and filtered by the site's country. This provides the
`iNat_nativeness` (e.g. `native`, `introduced`) and `iNat_authority`
fields.

**From EASIN** — the
[European Alien Species Information Network](https://easin.jrc.ec.europa.eu/easin)
API is queried for each taxon by scientific name, returning additional
alien species attributes when the taxon is present in the EASIN catalogue:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `EASIN_url` | Link to the EASIN species factsheet |
| `EASIN_id` | EASIN species identifier |
| `EASIN_LSID` | Life Science Identifier (`urn:lsid:easin.jrc.ec.europa.eu:species:...`) |
| `EASIN_firstIntroductionsInEU_year` | Year of first recorded introduction in the EU |
| `EASIN_firstIntroductions_Country` | Country of first recorded introduction in the EU |
| `EASIN_status` | Alien status code (`A` = Alien, `Q` = Cryptogenic, `C` = Questionable) |
| `EASIN_hasImpact` | Whether a documented ecological impact is recorded (`True`/`False`) |
| `EASIN_IsEUConcern` | Whether listed as a species of EU concern under Regulation (EU) No 1143/2014 (`True`/`False`) |

All EASIN fields are `NA` when the taxon is not present in the EASIN
catalogue (i.e. it is not considered an alien species in Europe).

> **Note:** EASIN reports alien status at the country level and does not
> distinguish sub-national cases where a species may be non-native only in
> specific areas (e.g. islands) but native elsewhere within the same country.
> EASIN information may therefore overgeneralise nativeness for
> heterogeneous territories such as Italy.

```{r step5}
occ_eLTER_nativeness <- add_nativeness_to_occ(
  occ_eLTER = occ_eLTER_IUCN,
  country   = country
)
```

```
# Example content of establishmentMeans[[1]] for a native species:
# A tibble: 1 × 11
#   iNat_nativeness iNat_authority   iNat_checkList_uri EASIN_url EASIN_id ...
#   <chr>           <chr>            <chr>              <chr>     <chr>
# 1 native          Italy Check List https://www.in...  NA        NA        ...
#
# Example content of establishmentMeans[[1]] for an alien species:
# A tibble: 1 × 11
#   iNat_nativeness iNat_authority   iNat_checkList_uri EASIN_url            EASIN_id ...
#   <chr>           <chr>            <chr>              <chr>                <chr>
# 1 introduced      Italy Check List https://www.in...  https://easin.jrc... 1234      ...
```

### Step 6 — Add EU legal framework (EUNIS)

`add_eunis_legal_to_occ()` queries the [EUNIS species website](https://eunis.eea.europa.eu)
and appends `directive` and `annex` columns indicating coverage under the EU Habitats
Directive (92/43/EEC) or the EU Birds Directive (2009/147/EC).

```{r step6}
occ_eLTER_legal <- add_eunis_legal_to_occ(occ_eLTER = occ_eLTER_nativeness)
```

### Step 7 — Create the interactive map

`create_leaflet_occ_map()` produces an interactive Leaflet map with
colour-coded markers by iconic taxon group, clustering, and rich popups
showing all enriched attributes for each observation.

```{r step7}
map <- create_leaflet_occ_map(
  occ_enriched  = occ_eLTER_legal,
  site_boundary = site_boundary
)
map
```

The popup for each observation includes:

- Taxon name (linked to iNaturalist) and common name
- Observer and direct link to the observation record
- Observation quality grade, geoprivacy, and positional accuracy
- IUCN Red List status per geographic scope, with links to Red List assessments
- Nativeness and authority from iNaturalist national checklist
- EASIN alien species data (factsheet link, status, impact, EU concern, first introduction)
- EU Directive coverage and relevant Annex, with links to EUR-Lex
